_The second KICK ETF offers U.S. investors index-based exposure to the data center hardware and space infrastructure companies that may one day support computing in orbit._

OKLAHOMA CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC ("ETC") and Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. today announced the launch of the KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF (Nasdaq: SDC), the second fund in the KICK ETFs lineup. SDC joins the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (NYSE Arca: KCHP), which began trading on September 15, 2026.

AI is putting growing pressure on power grids. The International Energy Agency projects that global data center electricity demand will more than double by 2030, and grid connections have become a constraint for some new builds.1 That pressure has led some companies to explore whether data centers could one day operate in orbit, where certain orbits could offer near-constant sunlight, radiative cooling and no need for land.2,3 In October 2026, Google launched a prototype satellite carrying its AI chips and reported running an AI model on it in orbit.4,5 Starcloud, a privately held startup, has reported in December 2025 that it has trained an AI model on a GPU in space.6 The concept remains early-stage, with unresolved challenges in launch costs, radiation, maintenance and commercial viability.7

Putting computing in orbit would take more than a satellite. Data center hardware must process, move and store data, and space infrastructure would need to carry and support the equipment. SDC seeks to track, before fees and expenses, the Akros Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ("the Index"), which holds up to 30 U.S.-listed companies across those two areas: data center hardware, including compute, networking and interconnect, and memory and storage; and space infrastructure, including launch, satellites and spacecraft, satellite services and ground equipment. Many of these companies may also serve ground data centers and other markets. Inclusion in the Index does not by itself mean a company operates an orbital data center or earns revenue from one.

"Investors are being asked to make sense of AI infrastructure at a time when it is spreading in more directions than ever," said Garrett Stevens, Co-Founder and Chief Business Officer of Exchange Traded Concepts. "We believe they are better served when they know exactly which part of the buildout they own. KCHP offered investors focused access to Korea's semiconductor industry. SDC seeks to apply the same discipline to an earlier-stage frontier: the effort to extend data infrastructure into space."

"Most of the conversation about AI infrastructure stays on the ground, with the chips, the power and the buildings," said Yoon Gu Eric Lee, President and Chief Executive Officer of Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. "The companies building the hardware and space systems that could support computing in orbit deserve a place in that conversation. With SDC, U.S. investors can access that segment through a rules-based index in a familiar ETF format."

The Index is owned, calculated, administered and published by Akros Technologies, Inc. Akros ranks companies using NEXUS, its proprietary rubric-based framework that evaluates how central each company's business is to the Index theme. An Index committee reviews constituents for continued eligibility. The Index is reconstituted and rebalanced quarterly.

The Index treats data center hardware and space infrastructure as separate sleeves and targets 15 companies in each. Each sleeve's share of Index weight is set by its number of constituents at every quarterly rebalance, and within each sleeve, companies are weighted by free-float market capitalization. Holdings and weights shift between rebalances, and current holdings are published daily at kicketfs.com/sdc.

SDC seeks to track its Index by holding the stocks in the Index. Investors can buy and sell shares of the Fund through a standard brokerage account.

Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. Founded in 2000, Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. is a Korea-based financial services company offering securities brokerage, investment trading, discretionary investment and advisory services. The company is a core member of the Daou Kiwoom Group and serves investors through its online financial platform. Learn more about the parent company at www.kiwoom.com/h/ir/en/main and the KICK ETFs at www.KICKETFS.com.

Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC is an SEC-registered independent investment adviser specializing in white-label ETFs, sub-advisory services, portfolio management, fund marketing and consulting services. ETC helps asset managers bring ETF strategies to market efficiently and cost-effectively through the ETF structure. Learn more at www.exchangetradedconcepts.com.

The Fund is a series of Exchange Listed Funds Trust. Distributed by Foreside Fund Services, LLC. Foreside, Exchange Traded Concepts, Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. and Akros Technologies, Inc. are unaffiliated companies. KICK is a service mark of Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. and has been licensed for use by Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC, the Fund's adviser.

Investing involves risk, including possible loss of principal. Because the Fund is "non-diversified," it may invest a greater percentage of its assets in the securities of a single issuer or a lesser number of issuers than if it were a diversified fund, which may increase volatility. The Fund invests in space-related and information technology companies. Space-related companies may be harmed by launch failures, deployment malfunctions, mission delays, and cost overruns. _두 번째 KICK ETF는 미국 투자자들에게 언젠가 궤도 컴퓨팅을 지원할 데이터 센터 하드웨어 및 우주 인프라 회사에 대한 지수 기반 노출을 제공한다._

오클라호마시티, 2026년 11월 18일 /PRNewswire/ -- Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC("ETC")와 Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc.는 오늘 KICK ETF 라인업의 두 번째 펀드인 KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF(Nasdaq: SDC)의 출시를 발표했다. SDC는 2026년 9월 15일 거래를 시작한 KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (NYSE Arca: KCHP)에 합류했다.

AI는 전력망에 점점 더 큰 압력을 가하고 있다. 국제 에너지 기구(International Energy Agency)는 전 세계 데이터 센터 전력 수요가 2030년까지 두 배 이상 증가할 것으로 예상하고 있으며, 일부 새로운 구축에서는 그리드 연결이 제약이 될 것으로 예상한다.1 이러한 압력으로 인해 일부 기업은 언젠가 데이터 센터가 궤도에서 운영될 수 있는지 탐구하게 되었다. 특정 궤도는 거의 일정한 햇빛과 복사 냉각을 제공하며 토지가 필요하지 않다.2,3 2026년 10월 Google은 AI 칩을 탑재한 프로토타입 위성을 발사하고 궤도에서 AI 모델을 실행한다고 보고했다.4,5 개최된 스타트업은 2025년 12월 우주의 GPU에서 AI 모델을 훈련했다고 보고했다.6 이 개념은 아직 초기 단계로, 발사 비용, 방사선, 유지 관리 및 상업적 생존 가능성 측면에서 해결되지 않은 문제가 있다.7

컴퓨팅을 궤도에 올리려면 위성보다 더 많은 것이 필요한다. 데이터 센터 하드웨어는 데이터를 처리, 이동 및 저장해야 하며 공간 인프라는 장비를 운반하고 지원해야 한다. SDC는 수수료 및 비용을 지불하기 전에 Akros Space 데이터 센터 및 인프라 지수("지수")를 추적하려고 한다. 이 지수에는 컴퓨팅, 네트워킹 및 상호 연결, 메모리 및 스토리지를 포함한 데이터 센터 하드웨어, 두 영역에 걸쳐 최대 30개의 미국 상장 회사가 포함되어 있다. 발사, 위성 및 우주선, 위성 서비스 및 지상 장비를 포함한 우주 인프라. 이들 회사 중 다수는 지상 데이터 센터 및 기타 시장에도 서비스를 제공할 수 있다. 지수에 포함된다고 해서 회사가 궤도 데이터 센터를 운영하거나 그곳에서 수익을 얻는다는 의미는 아닙니다.

Exchange Traded Concepts의 공동 창립자이자 최고 비즈니스 책임자인 Garrett Stevens는 "AI 인프라가 그 어느 때보다 다양한 방향으로 확산되고 있는 시점에서 투자자들은 AI 인프라를 이해하도록 요구받고 있다."라고 말했다. "우리는 그들이 소유한 구축 부분을 정확히 알 때 더 나은 서비스를 받을 수 있다고 믿다. KCHP는 투자자들에게 한국의 반도체 산업에 대한 집중적인 접근을 제공했다. SDC는 데이터 인프라를 우주로 확장하려는 노력이라는 초기 단계의 개척에 동일한 원칙을 적용하려고 한다."
